title: Installation: a Docker machine of your own, and Docker Desktop

videos.script: Every command from here on is typed on a machine you build yourself. {{machine}} There are three ways to get one: installed, in a virtual machine, or online. This course recommends the virtual machine: an Ubuntu made by Multipass, with Docker Engine inside. It is the same shape as the one every transcript came from, and you can throw it away. {{vm}} Then Docker Desktop, which most people meet first on a laptop. It is a Linux virtual machine with Docker inside. Your containers run in that VM, not on Windows and not on the Mac. The docker command stays on your side, and sends each request in. {{install}} Installing it is three steps on every system. What changes is the step that fails: virtualisation switched off on Windows, the wrong installer on a Mac. {{checks}} Then four checks. Two halves answer docker version. Hello world runs. The context says which engine you are talking to. And docker info says how big the machine is, which is the real limit on your containers. {{fails}} Last, what goes wrong, and what each message means. A group that needs a new login. A pull limit. A network that inspects encrypted traffic. A port somebody else holds. And when nothing makes sense any more, you delete the machine and build it again.
